title: DEIM-L vs RT-DETR-X: benchmark on one protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: accuracy ties at 57.8 vs 57.9 mAP, but DEIM-L reaches it with half the parameters and 245 vs 401 MB peak VRAM.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: Accuracy is a tie: DEIM-L and RT-DETR-X land at 57.8 vs 57.9 mAP@50-95 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, 0.1 points apart. DEIM-L reaches that mark with far fewer parameters and 245 vs 401 MB peak VRAM. RT-DETR-X is 14% faster on this GPU in PyTorch, but the order reverses on TensorRT FP32 and Jetson Orin. When the two are this close on accuracy, efficiency decides.

DEIM-L (31.24M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-X (67.37M, Apache-2.0) are both transformer detectors evaluated at 640 px input on COCO val2017. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU and Jetson Orin. RT-DETR-X carries more than twice the parameters for the same measured accuracy.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-L and RT-DETR-X highlighted against the full set of measured models.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. DEIM-L measures 57.8 mAP@50-95 and RT-DETR-X 57.9, close enough to call a tie. DEIM-L leads on small objects: 45.2 vs 39.8 mAP_small, a 13.56% relative gap. Measured against compute, DEIM-L extracts 156% more mAP per GFLOP.

On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-X is 14.52% faster in PyTorch (21.8 vs 18.6 FPS). That is where its speed lead ends. On ONNX Runtime DEIM-L leads 50.5 vs 48.4 FPS, on TensorRT FP32 75.7 vs 68.5 FPS, and on Jetson Orin 4.8 vs 3.0 FPS.
The speed answer is not portable. RT-DETR-X wins only on desktop PyTorch; DEIM-L is faster on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT FP32, and Jetson Orin. Benchmark on your own runtime before choosing.

Pick DEIM-L for the same accuracy at lower cost: fewer parameters, less peak VRAM at 245 vs 401 MB, and faster inference on every runtime except desktop PyTorch. Pick RT-DETR-X only if desktop PyTorch throughput is the single constraint. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMl.pt")     # 31.24M params, 57.8 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRx.pt") # 67.37M params, 57.9 mAP@50-95

results = deim("image.jpg")
